boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented Winona-campus spaces for studying, collaborating, recreation, performance, and everyday student connection.

cards.title: Set up at the Reference Room
cards.subtitle: Fitzgerald Library, main level
cards.notes: Bring a laptop or a study partner and use the long tables, outlet access, chairs, or nearby computers on the library’s main level.
cards.short_summary: A main-level library workspace with tables, power, seating, and computers.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s identifies the Reference Room as a main-level Fitzgerald Library space with chairs, long tables near power outlets, and computers.
cards.source_title: Winona Study Spaces | Saint Mary's Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located in Fitzgerald Library on the Winona campus; check the library’s current hours before going.

cards.title: Meet in McEnery Lounge
cards.subtitle: Fitzgerald Library, first floor
cards.notes: Use this first-floor lounge when your group needs room to spread out, talk through an assignment, or work alongside other students.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor collaborative lounge in Fitzgerald Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s describes McEnery Lounge as a first-floor collaborative environment for individual and group study activities.
cards.source_title: Winona Study Spaces | Saint Mary's Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located in Fitzgerald Library; library access and room availability may vary.

cards.title: Reserve a group study room
cards.subtitle: Fitzgerald Library
cards.notes: Reserve one of the library’s group rooms when you need a defined place to rehearse, plan, or focus together on coursework.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms intended for group study.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says Fitzgerald Library has numerous study rooms that students can reserve for group study.
cards.source_title: Winona Study Spaces | Saint Mary's Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required; use the library’s study-room reservation information.

cards.title: Use McEnery Classroom 33 between classes
cards.subtitle: Fitzgerald Library, lower level
cards.notes: Check whether class is in session, then use Classroom 33 as an extra lower-level work setting for reading, drafting, or group prep.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level McEnery classroom available to students outside scheduled classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says students may use McEnery Classroom 33 whenever classes are not in session.
cards.source_title: Winona Study Spaces | Saint Mary's Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available only when classes are not in session.

cards.title: Check Classroom 39 for open work time
cards.subtitle: Fitzgerald Library, lower level
cards.notes: Look for an unscheduled window and use Classroom 39 as a practical alternative workspace when the rest of the library feels busy.
cards.short_summary: A second lower-level McEnery classroom open outside class sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says students may use McEnery Classroom 39 whenever classes are not in session.
cards.source_title: Winona Study Spaces | Saint Mary's Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available only when classes are not in session.

cards.title: Take a quieter seat upstairs
cards.subtitle: Fitzgerald Library, Upper McEnery
cards.notes: Choose a chair or table in Upper McEnery when you want a quieter library change of scene, with computers and a printer nearby.
cards.short_summary: An upper-level library area with seating, tables, computers, and printing.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s lists the Upper McEnery Study Area with chairs, tables, two PCs, and a printer.
cards.source_title: Winona Study Spaces | Saint Mary's Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located in Fitzgerald Library; check current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Work in The Pit
cards.subtitle: Fitzgerald Library, Lower McEnery
cards.notes: Use The Pit when you need a Mac, scanner, printer, or a study table; it is a practical stop for production-focused course work.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level lab with Macs, scanning, printing, and study tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says the Lower McEnery Lab, called “The Pit,” has four Mac computers, a printer, scanner, and study tables.
cards.source_title: Winona Study Spaces | Saint Mary's Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located in Fitzgerald Library; equipment availability may vary.

cards.title: Claim a study carrel
cards.subtitle: Fitzgerald Library, all floors
cards.notes: Pick a carrel when you need concentrated solo time, then use the library’s three-floor layout to find the level that suits your task.
cards.short_summary: Individual study carrels distributed throughout the library.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s states that Fitzgerald Library offers study carrels on all floors for concentrated study.
cards.source_title: Winona Study Spaces | Saint Mary's Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located in Fitzgerald Library; check current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Orient around Toner Student Center
cards.subtitle: Winona campus student center
cards.notes: Use the center as a campus waypoint for dining, the bookstore, games, lounge time, and student support offices; confirm each service’s availability.
cards.short_summary: A central student-services building with dining, lounge, games, bookstore, and support offices.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Winona campus map lists Michael H. Toner Student Center with dining areas, a lounge, game room, bookstore, and student-support services.
cards.source_title: Saint Mary’s University of Minnesota Winona Campus Map
cards.access_notes: On the Winona campus; individual dining, bookstore, game-room, and office access may vary.

cards.title: Find a performance at the Performance Center
cards.subtitle: Winona campus
cards.notes: Check the university calendar, then use the Performance Center’s named theatre, recital, studio, and lobby venues as a starting point for campus arts events.
cards.short_summary: The campus performance building includes theatre, recital, studio, and lobby venues.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Winona campus map lists the Performance Center with Joseph Page Theatre, Figliulo Recital Hall, Studio Theatre, and Ben Miller Lobby.
cards.source_title: Saint Mary’s University of Minnesota Winona Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Event access depends on the scheduled performance or campus activity.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten named public outdoor destinations in Winona for an easy walk, conversation, or self-guided explore without admission or a purchase.

cards.title: Walk the Bluffside Park Trails
cards.subtitle: Bluffside Park, Winona
cards.notes: Pick a marked segment, set a turnaround point, and walk it together. Stay on maintained routes and adjust plans for weather and trail conditions.
cards.short_summary: A self-paced trail walk in the city-maintained Bluffside system.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Winona lists Bluffside Park trails under outdoor recreation and states that all areas are free unless noted.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Recreation | City of Winona
cards.access_notes: City outdoor-recreation page says all areas are free unless noted; use the posted trail map and observe conditions.

cards.title: Take a Prairie Island Trail Loop
cards.subtitle: Prairie Island Trail, Winona
cards.notes: Use the city trail map to choose a short loop, bring water, and make it a low-key catch-up walk with a view of the surrounding backwaters.
cards.short_summary: A mapped soft-surface trail for a no-cost outdoor meet-up.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Winona includes the Prairie Island Trail Map in its outdoor-recreation resources and states that all areas are free unless noted.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Recreation | City of Winona
cards.access_notes: City outdoor-recreation page says all areas are free unless noted; use the map and respect posted trail guidance.

cards.title: Hike the Sugar Loaf Trail
cards.subtitle: Sugar Loaf, Winona
cards.notes: Plan a daylight hike with sturdy shoes, pause at safe viewpoints, and head back before dark. Follow the city map instead of making an off-trail route.
cards.short_summary: A mapped Sugar Loaf outing that costs nothing to access.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Winona provides a Sugar Loaf and Winona Ice Park map within its outdoor-recreation resources and states that all areas are free unless noted.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Recreation | City of Winona
cards.access_notes: City outdoor-recreation page says all areas are free unless noted; hike only marked routes and check conditions.

cards.title: Circle Part of East Lake
cards.subtitle: East Lake Path, Winona
cards.notes: Meet at a convenient access point and walk or roll a section of the paved lakeside path. The full East Lake route is listed as 3.7 miles.
cards.short_summary: A paved lakeside route suited to a flexible-length hang.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Winona lists East Lake as a 3.7-mile path and states that all outdoor-recreation areas are free unless noted.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Recreation | City of Winona
cards.access_notes: City outdoor-recreation page says all areas are free unless noted; share the path and use normal road-crossing care.

cards.title: Do a West Lake Path Stroll
cards.subtitle: West Lake Path, Winona
cards.notes: Use this shorter paved route for a quick walk between classes or a relaxed conversation. The city lists the West Lake path at 1.8 miles.
cards.short_summary: A shorter lake-path option for an unhurried walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Winona lists West Lake as a 1.8-mile path and states that all outdoor-recreation areas are free unless noted.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Recreation | City of Winona
cards.access_notes: City outdoor-recreation page says all areas are free unless noted; keep pets leashed where required and follow posted rules.

cards.title: Walk or Bike the Flyway Trail
cards.subtitle: Flyway Trail, Winona
cards.notes: Choose an out-and-back section and trade playlist picks or class updates as you go. Use the city map and yield appropriately on the shared route.
cards.short_summary: A mapped paved trail for walking or using a bike you already have.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Winona includes the Flyway Trail Map among its paved-trail resources and states that all areas are free unless noted.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Recreation | City of Winona
cards.access_notes: City outdoor-recreation page says all areas are free unless noted; cycling requires your own equipment and safe riding practices.

cards.title: Follow the Downtown River Trail
cards.subtitle: Mississippi River Trail - Downtown Winona
cards.notes: Use the downtown trail map for a walk beside the river, then stop at a public overlook to talk or take photos without needing to buy anything.
cards.short_summary: A city-mapped downtown route along the Mississippi corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Winona provides a Mississippi River Trail - Downtown Winona map and states that all outdoor-recreation areas are free unless noted.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Recreation | City of Winona
cards.access_notes: City outdoor-recreation page says all areas are free unless noted; follow the map and use designated crossings.

cards.title: Meet Up at Levee Park
cards.subtitle: Levee Park, downtown Winona
cards.notes: Bring a friend for a seated riverfront conversation or a slow loop through the park. It is also one of the city locations with free public wireless internet.
cards.short_summary: A public riverfront park with free city Wi-Fi.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Winona identifies Levee Park as a free public wireless hotspot and describes it among the city's public locations.
cards.source_title: Wireless Hot Spots | City of Winona
cards.access_notes: The city provides free public Wi-Fi at Levee Park; park access does not require admission or a purchase.

cards.title: Sit and Sketch at Lake Park
cards.subtitle: Lake Park, Winona
cards.notes: Bring a notebook or sketchpad you already own, settle in at the park, and swap observations. Keep the plan to the public park rather than rentals or paid facilities.
cards.short_summary: A named city park for a bring-your-own creative break.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Winona lists Lake Park in its parks and playgrounds inventory; its outdoor-recreation page states that all areas are free unless noted.
cards.source_title: Parks & Playgrounds | City of Winona
cards.access_notes: Use the public park areas only; the city notes that outdoor-recreation areas are free unless specifically noted otherwise.

cards.title: Explore Aghaming Park Preserve
cards.subtitle: Aghaming Park Preserve, Winona
cards.notes: Make a daylight nature walk with a friend and keep to open, designated public areas. Leave wildlife and plants undisturbed and pack out anything you bring.
cards.short_summary: A named Winona park preserve for a quiet, no-cost outdoor walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Winona lists Aghaming Park Preserve in its parks and playgrounds inventory; its outdoor-recreation page states that all areas are free unless noted.
cards.source_title: Parks & Playgrounds | City of Winona
cards.access_notes: Use designated public areas and follow posted preserve guidance; the city lists outdoor-recreation areas as free unless noted.

cards.access_notes: The surrounding park area remains public; reservations and individual event terms may differ.

cards.title: Watkins General Store
cards.subtitle: East Third Street corridor · entrance between Liberty and Chestnut
cards.notes: Enter from East Third Street to browse the museum displays on Watkins products, advertising, photos, and memorabilia.
cards.short_summary: A free-admission company museum and store with a Third Street entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Watkins states that its Winona General Store has free admission and that the museum-and-store entrance is on East Third Street between Liberty and Chestnut.
cards.source_title: Watkins General Store
cards.access_notes: Admission is explicitly free; retail products are optional purchases. Published hours vary by day.

cards.title: Winona Public Library
cards.subtitle: West Fifth Street corridor · 151 W 5th St
cards.notes: Use the West Fifth Street corridor for a library stop, and verify the seasonal Saturday schedule before you set out.
cards.short_summary: A named public library with published weekday and seasonal Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Winona Public Library lists its address as 151 W 5th St and publishes weekday and seasonal Saturday hours.
cards.source_title: Hours & Contact Info — Winona Public Library
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s published holiday closures and seasonal Saturday hours before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Saint Mary’s observances, recognitions, and service rituals tied to its Lasallian Catholic identity.

cards.title: De La Salle Week
cards.subtitle: Annual third-week-of-March heritage observance
cards.notes: Watch campus announcements in March, then choose an activity that helps you learn how Saint Mary’s connects its mission, history, and community.
cards.short_summary: A yearly week of changing events that leads into Founders’ Day.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s sets aside the third week of March each year for De La Salle Week to commemorate its Lasallian Catholic mission and heritage.
cards.source_title: Why do we celebrate De La Salle Week and Founders’ Day?
cards.access_notes: Activities vary by year; consult the university’s current event announcements.

cards.title: Founders’ Day
cards.subtitle: Annual March celebration of Saint Mary’s founders
cards.notes: Set aside the day’s shortened class schedule to attend the Mass or Convocation and see how the university marks its Lasallian roots.
cards.short_summary: The annual centerpiece honoring Bishop Heffron, De La Salle, and the Christian Brothers.
cards.evidence_claim: Founders’ Day is Saint Mary’s annual main event during De La Salle Week and honors Saint John Baptist de La Salle, Bishop Heffron, the Christian Brothers, and others pivotal to the university’s history.
cards.source_title: Why do we celebrate De La Salle Week and Founders’ Day?
cards.access_notes: The 2026 celebration was held March 17 on the Winona Campus; dates and program details vary annually.

cards.title: Founders’ Day Convocation
cards.subtitle: Page Theatre recognition gathering
cards.notes: Follow the annual program when released; the Convocation is the formal gathering where Saint Mary’s recognizes mission-centered contributions and seniors.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial program within Founders’ Day that brings recognitions together.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s held its 2026 Founders’ Day Convocation in Page Theatre on the Winona Campus and provided a livestream option.
cards.source_title: Founders’ Day 2026 Convocation Livestream Link
cards.access_notes: Venue, streaming, and start time are announced with each year’s program.

cards.title: The Lasallian Educator Honor
cards.subtitle: Annual Founders’ Day recognition
cards.notes: Read the recipient citation when it is announced; it is a useful window into the teaching and service values Saint Mary’s publicly celebrates.
cards.short_summary: An annual award for a faculty, staff, or administration member living Lasallian ideals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Distinguished Lasallian Educator Award is presented each year at Saint Mary’s to recognize a faculty, staff, or administration member who exemplifies the ideals of Saint John Baptist de La Salle.
cards.source_title: Four honored during Saint Mary’s Founders’ Day celebration
cards.access_notes: Award announcements are part of the annual Founders’ Day program.

cards.title: The Heffron Award
cards.subtitle: Biennial service-and-commitment recognition
cards.notes: Look for this honor in Founders’ Day coverage every other year and read the recipient profile for examples of long-term university service.
cards.short_summary: A Founders’ Day award named for Saint Mary’s founder.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bishop Patrick Heffron Award is given every other year to an employee who has positively contributed to university life and modeled the Lasallian spirit.
cards.source_title: Four honored during Saint Mary’s Founders’ Day celebration
cards.access_notes: Presented every other year as part of Founders’ Day recognition.

cards.title: Outstanding Senior Recognition
cards.subtitle: Founders’ Day senior honor
cards.notes: Check the nominee list and Convocation program each March to see which graduating students are recognized for scholarship, character, leadership, and service.
cards.short_summary: A yearly recognition of graduating seniors during Founders’ Day.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s announces Outstanding Male and Female Seniors during Founders’ Day; recipients are selected for scholarship, character, leadership, service, and concern for others.
cards.source_title: Four honored during Saint Mary’s Founders’ Day celebration
cards.access_notes: Nominees and awardees are announced through the annual Founders’ Day program.

cards.title: Lasallian Day of Service
cards.subtitle: Annual October community-service day
cards.notes: Register for a listed project or organize a qualifying local service activity during October, following the current university sign-up instructions.
cards.short_summary: A Saint Mary’s community day for hands-on service near and far.
cards.evidence_claim: Lasallian Day of Service is typically held on one of the last non-holiday Saturdays in October and brings Saint Mary’s alumni, students, faculty, staff, and friends together for service projects.
cards.source_title: Lasallian Day of Service Home
cards.access_notes: The official page lists the next event as October 24, 2026; project locations and registration are posted there.

cards.entity_name: Feast of the Immaculate Conception – Patronal Feast Day
cards.title: Saint Mary’s Patronal Feast
cards.subtitle: December 8 observance of the university’s patroness
cards.notes: Check Campus Ministry’s current schedule for the Mass or observance, and use the occasion to learn why Mary’s feast is important to the university.
cards.short_summary: A December observance connected directly to the university’s namesake and Catholic identity.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s identifies the Feast of the Immaculate Conception as its Patronal Feast Day and lists it annually on December 8.
cards.source_title: Feast of the Immaculate Conception – Patronal Feast Day
cards.access_notes: The university calendar lists the observance on December 8, 2026; confirm service details with Campus Ministry.

cards.title: Pre-finals Late Night Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Annual Winona Campus study-season gathering
cards.notes: Watch the holiday-season calendar for the current date and location, then take a study break with the campus community before finals begin.
cards.short_summary: A recurring late-evening breakfast event held ahead of final exams.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s describes its Winona Campus pre-finals late night breakfast as an annual tradition and documents students and staff participating.
cards.source_title: Holiday
cards.access_notes: The official page confirms the annual event but does not publish current hours; check current campus announcements.

cards.title: Baccalaureate Before Commencement
cards.subtitle: Graduation-morning liturgy at Saint Thomas More Chapel
cards.notes: If you are graduating or supporting a graduate, review the current commencement page for the morning Mass details before the ceremony begins.
cards.short_summary: A Lasallian Catholic graduation-morning liturgy of thanksgiving.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s holds a Baccalaureate Mass on the morning of undergraduate Commencement as a liturgy of thanksgiving for graduates and their families, welcoming people of all faith traditions.
cards.source_title: Winona Undergraduate Commencement
cards.access_notes: Held on the morning of Commencement; current ceremony details are published on the university commencement page.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Saint Mary's University of Minnesota, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend sequence that starts on the Winona campus and opens into public cultural and outdoor destinations around town.

cards.title: Start at Toner Student Center
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · campus orientation point
cards.notes: Use the student center as your first indoor waypoint: get your bearings, then look for campus information or a public gathering before choosing the next stop.
cards.short_summary: A central campus starting point with meeting, dining, and lounge spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s lists the Michael H. Toner Student Center on its Winona campus map and identifies meeting rooms, dining areas, a bookstore, and a game room there.
cards.source_title: Saint Mary’s University of Minnesota Winona Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Campus map identifies the building; check current campus access and event information before visiting.

cards.title: Make Fitzgerald Library your reset stop
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Winona campus
cards.notes: Drop in with a friend to find a calm study setting, ask about materials, or simply use the library as a clear landmark while you learn the campus layout.
cards.short_summary: The Winona campus library is a reliable place to pause and orient yourself.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s Libraries identifies Fitzgerald Library as the Winona library at 700 Terrace Heights #26.
cards.source_title: Winona Hours & Location | Saint Mary’s Libraries
cards.access_notes: See the library’s current hours page before going; access and services may vary.

cards.title: Find Saint Thomas More Chapel
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · campus landmark
cards.notes: Add the chapel to a self-guided campus walk. Read the nearby signage or pause outside, and check Campus Ministry for any current public worship information.
cards.short_summary: A named campus chapel that also anchors university ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s campus map lists Saint Thomas More Chapel, and the university’s 2026 Founders’ Day program located Mass there.
cards.source_title: Founders’ Day Celebrations | Saint Mary’s Today
cards.access_notes: Treat this as a campus landmark; confirm any worship or building-access details with Campus Ministry.

cards.title: Check what is on at Page Theatre
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Performance Center
cards.notes: Look for a current performance or public arts listing, then reserve only if required. If nothing is scheduled, use the Performance Center as a campus landmark on your walk.
cards.short_summary: A campus performance venue used for university arts programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s identifies Joseph Page Theatre in the Performance Center, and its 2026 Shakespeare Showcase took place there with free general admission and required reservations.
cards.source_title: Saint Mary’s University partners with Great River Shakespeare Festival for student showcase
cards.access_notes: Event availability, admission, and reservations vary; confirm the current listing before making plans.

cards.title: Walk by David R. Thies B’59 Arena
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · campus athletics
cards.notes: Use the arena as a waypoint on an after-dinner campus loop. Check the university’s athletics or events calendar if you want to pair the walk with a scheduled activity.
cards.short_summary: The renamed Winona campus gymnasium is a major athletics landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s announced that its Winona campus gymnasium would be named the David R. Thies B’59 Arena.
cards.source_title: Alumnus leaves lasting mark on Saint Mary’s
cards.access_notes: Building access and event entry depend on current university scheduling and policies.

cards.title: Spot the soccer field on a campus loop
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · outdoor campus stop
cards.notes: Take a daylight walk past the field and nearby athletic facilities. Keep to established campus routes and use the campus map to connect this stop with the rest of your loop.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor athletic field on the Winona campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s Winona campus map labels the Leo Ochrymowycz Memorial Soccer Field among its outdoor recreation facilities.
cards.source_title: Saint Mary’s University of Minnesota Winona Campus Map
cards.access_notes: View from public campus routes; field access depends on athletics scheduling.

cards.title: Take a Lake Winona Path walk
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Lake Park
cards.notes: Choose a comfortable out-and-back segment for a first visit. Stay alert for pedestrians, skaters, and cyclists sharing the paved route, then turn around before dark.
cards.short_summary: A paved loop around East and West Lake Winona for walking or cycling.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Winona describes Lake Winona Path as a five-mile blacktop trail through Lake Park that circles both lake segments and is used by pedestrians, skaters, and cyclists.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Recreation | City of Winona
cards.access_notes: The city advises users to be alert because the path is shared by multiple types of travelers.

cards.title: Save Garvin Heights for a daylight view
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Winona blufftop
cards.notes: Go in daylight with water and suitable shoes. Use the city’s listed trailhead and steps information to decide whether the short uphill route fits your group’s comfort level.
cards.short_summary: A city park with blufftop views and hiking paths through native ecosystems.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Winona says Garvin Heights Park has hiking paths, a blufftop view, and a 0.4-mile trail with 378 man-made steps on its upper portion.
cards.source_title: Garvin Heights Park | City of Winona
cards.access_notes: The city lists a paved parking area and public-use picnic tables; use the marked trailhead and check conditions before hiking.

cards.title: Plan a water-inspired art stop
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · 800 Riverview Drive
cards.notes: Check current gallery hours and admission before heading over. If Sunday works for your schedule, give yourself time to explore the museum rather than rushing through it.
cards.short_summary: A Winona museum with art focused on water and the surrounding river setting.
cards.evidence_claim: MMAM lists museum hours Tuesday through Sunday, its Winona address, and a $7 student general-admission price; it also offers free student admission on Thursdays.
cards.source_title: Hours, Admission and Location | Minnesota Marine Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Current hours are Tuesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; student admission is listed separately, so verify any changes before visiting.

cards.title: End with local history at the Armory
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · 160 Johnson Street
cards.notes: Set aside an unhurried final stop for exhibits and the lobby gallery. Check the History Center’s visit page before leaving campus for current exhibit and access updates.
cards.short_summary: A historical museum in Winona’s 1915 National Guard Armory.
cards.evidence_claim: The Winona County Historical Society says the History Center is located in the historic 1915 National Guard Armory at 160 Johnson Street and lists daily museum-exhibit hours.
cards.source_title: Visit Our Museums | Winona County Historical Society
cards.access_notes: The visit page lists daily 10 a.m.–4 p.m. hours and $3 student admission; confirm exhibits and hours before arrival.
